long_biography.plain_text:
Banco Intercontinental placed Ramón Báez Figueroa at the centre of Dominican finance after he bought his father's stake and assumed the presidency. The bank had grown from a family-founded institution into a major private lender, aided by its acquisition of the healthier assets of Banco del Comercio.

Its growth masked accounts concealed from regulators. A Dominican appellate judgment found that Báez Figueroa and another executive diverted bank capital through overdrafts and a parallel accounting system, using the funds for linked companies. The Supreme Court made his ten-year sentence irrevocable in 2008. Released conditionally after five years and nine months, he later agreed to facilitate recovery of assets and abandon outstanding claims.
